xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3076: Polyrepo verdict anchors: 5 wrapper-blind stamp/compare sites need the composite HeadAnchor fix (stamp + compare together)

plan.title: Polyrepo verdict anchors: 5 wrapper-blind stamp/compare sites need the composite HeadAnchor fix (stamp + compare together)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Verdict anchors (reviewedAtCommit, lastVerifiedCommit, roleRunHead) are plain strings, so a composite polyrepo anchor (fe@sha api@sha) and a frozen wrapper-repo SHA are silently interchangeable. Five wrapper-blind stamp/compare sites therefore either loop forever (composite anchor vs wrapper HEAD never equal — MIN-901: 56 review resets + convoy re-dispatches in 3h44m) or ship unreviewed code green (wrapper anchor vs wrapper HEAD always equal — post-review sub-repo commits never invalidate review).
narratives.Proposal: Introduce a branded HeadAnchor type in src/lib/git-utils.ts with snapshotWorkspaceHeadsPromise() as the single producer and an exported parseCompositeSnapshot as the single lenient parser. Add a composite-aware drift evaluator applying per-repo benign-move checks (tree-identical, state-plane-only, patch-id-identical). Convert all five stamp/compare sites in this one branch (deacon checkPostReviewCommits; roleRunHead stamp+compare pair; the review-status route, legacy specialists-done route, and deacon bypass stamps), plus the two degraded sites (review runId derivation, crash progressFingerprint). Lock the write-site inventory with a targeted scan test. Full details, decisions D1-D9, and verified line references are in the PRD draft (drafts/pan-3076.md).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to the independent read-only probes owned by PAN-3037 (sync-main, review-restart branch detection, dashboard git status, start verification)
- No repo-wide grep/CI guard on 'git rev-parse HEAD' (explicitly rejected by the issue — many legitimate per-repo uses)
- No branding of the contracts wire Schema (packages/contracts/src/types.ts) or frontend types
- No merging of parseWorkspaceHeadAnchor (strict git-show validator) into parseCompositeSnapshot
- No migration/rewrite of already-persisted anchor values; legacy values converge via one conservative reset at runtime
- No changes to merge-train, close-out, or verification-runner stamp sites already using the producer

autoDecisions.summary: Included the two 'degraded' sites (review-agent runId, service-crash progressFingerprint) in scope alongside the five stamp/compare sites.
autoDecisions.rationale: They are listed in this issue's body as part of the same coupled cluster, convert to the same producer, and are small diffs; deferring them would leave known wrapper-blind probes behind the same brand boundary this issue creates.

autoDecisions.summary: Brand enforcement at write doors only; contracts Schema and roleRunHead storage types stay plain string; plane-copy paths use a rehydrateHeadAnchor cast; roleRunHead writes locked by the scan test.
autoDecisions.rationale: Branding the wire Schema would ripple into the frontend and ~6 deserializers with zero enforcement gain, since stored values re-enter as plain strings anyway; the write door is where fabrication happens.

autoDecisions.summary: roleRunHead switches from short-8 wrapper SHA to the full producer anchor on both sides; persisted pre-fix values intentionally read as stale once after deploy.
autoDecisions.rationale: Stale-once costs at most one redundant respawn; the current polyrepo behavior (staleness never fires) is the bug being fixed, and equality-only comparison needs no short form.

autoDecisions.summary: Mixed legacy anchor shapes (wrapper SHA stored, composite current) evaluate as 'drifted' — one conservative full re-review, then convergence.
autoDecisions.rationale: There is no repoKey mapping between shapes, so benign-move analysis is impossible; a single reset is the smallest safe outcome and the fixed stamp sites make it terminal.

autoDecisions.summary: Polyrepo review runId head8 = first 8 hex of sha1(composite anchor), derived by one helper shared by runId construction and the staleness probe.
autoDecisions.rationale: Any sub-repo commit must change the runId (roots[0]-only misses non-primary commits), and a shared helper makes stamp/compare divergence structurally impossible.

Do NOT touch parseWorkspaceHeadAnchor (git-utils.ts:278) — it stays a separate strict validator (decision D4).

Composite-aware workspace anchor drift evaluator with per-repo benign-move checks

expected_outputs: workspace-anchor-drift.test.ts passes with named tests for current/benign/drifted/shape-mismatch/unreadable verdicts

narrative.Action: Per PRD WI-2: create src/lib/workspace-anchor-drift.ts exporting evaluateWorkspaceAnchorDrift(issueId, workspacePath, storedAnchor) returning { kind: 'current' | 'benign' | 'drifted' | 'unreadable', currentAnchor?, changedRepos? }. Decision rules are fully specified in the PRD (steps 1-5): producer-undefined → unreadable; string-equal → current; two plain SHAs → today's workspace-root benign checks (^{tree} equality, haveSameEffectiveCodeCommit, haveSameCodeContribution from src/lib/pipeline-state-paths.ts:56,79); shape mismatch → drifted (decision D5); both composite → per-repoKey comparison with benign checks run in each changed root.dir using baseRef 'origin/' + root.targetBranch (decision D9). Unit tests use mkdtemp real git repos and vi.mock of resolveWorkspaceRepoRootsSync (pattern: tests/unit/lib/cloister/deacon-stash-janitor.test.ts).

items.title: Given equal stored and current composite anchors, evaluateWorkspaceAnchorDrift returns kind 'current'; given a commit in one sub-repo it returns 'drifted' naming that repoKey in changedRepos
Given a tree-identical rebase in exactly one sub-repo, the evaluator returns kind 'benign' with currentAnchor equal to the fresh producer snapshot
Given a stored plain wrapper SHA and a current composite snapshot (shape mismatch), the evaluator returns kind 'drifted', never loops, and never throws

Given two plain single-SHA anchors (monorepo), the evaluator reproduces today's workspace-root semantics: tree-identical or state-plane-only moves return 'benign', real code changes return 'drifted', unreadable workspace returns 'unreadable'
